data.why: The UI is entirely parametric (sliders/dropdowns for RPM, polymer/surfactant/crosslinker chemistry) with no file_uploader in app.py; it ships its own built-in configs (configs/default.toml, configs/fast_smoke.toml) and material property database (data/properties.toml) that are read directly from the repo, so nothing needs to be supplied as an upload.

goals: Set rotor-stator emulsification parameters (RPM, surfactant type/concentration) and predict the resulting droplet size distribution (d32, d50, span)
Tune gelation conditions (cooling rate, oil temperature, polymer concentrations) to hit a target pore size and porosity
Select a crosslinker and kinetics model, and project degree of conversion and network modulus over a given crosslinking time/temperature
Predict final double-network mechanical properties (shear modulus G_DN, effective modulus E*) for a chosen microsphere formulation
Compare platforms (agarose-chitosan, alginate, cellulose-NIPS, PLGA) to see which fabrication route best meets a target pore size or mechanical spec
Check the automated trust/reliability assessment to judge whether a given parameter combination falls within a well-evidenced regime before committing it to a wet-lab run

review.summary: The tree fits the M1 fabrication use well: the set-up, run, inspect, judge and bench-recipe phases match the README, and every screen I sampled supports its node. It omits crosslinker and formulation choice as tasks, the Scientific Mode switch, Monte Carlo uncertainty, and the whole M2/M3 functionalization and chromatography path, so it needs those fixes before filing.
